stem: The radii of two circles are 7 cm and 4 cm. If the distance between their centres is 8 cm, then the circles will

options.D: intersect each other at two points.

explanation: Let $r_1 = 7\text{ cm}, r_2 = 4\text{ cm}$, distance between centres $d = 8\text{ cm}$. Difference of radii $= |r_1 - r_2| = 7 - 4 = 3\text{ cm}$. Sum of radii $= r_1 + r_2 = 7 + 4 = 11\text{ cm}$. Since $|r_1 - r_2| < d < r_1 + r_2$ ($3 < 8 < 11$), the circles intersect each other at two distinct points.

stem:
In the given circle with centre $O$, if $PQ$ and $RS$ are equal chords, then the equal angles are

I. $\angle POQ = \angle ROS$
II. $\angle POR = \angle QOS$
III. $\angle ORS = \angle POQ$
explanation: Equal chords subtend equal central angles, so $\angle POQ = \angle ROS$ (I is true). Adding the common angle $\angle QOR$ to both sides gives $\angle POQ + \angle QOR = \angle ROS + \angle QOR \implies \angle POR = \angle QOS$ (II is true). Angle $\angle ORS$ is a base angle of an isosceles triangle, not equal to central angle $\angle POQ$. Thus I and II are equal.

The given diagram shows a circle having centre at $O$. The chord $AB$ and $BC$ are congruent.

If the length of chord $BC = \frac{1}{2}a\text{ cm}$, then the sum of lengths of chord $DE$ and chord $EF$ is
explanation: In the symmetric diagram with congruent chords: chord $AB = BC = \frac{1}{2}a\text{ cm}$. Chords $DE$ and $EF$ are congruent to $AB$ and $BC$ ($DE = EF = \frac{1}{2}a\text{ cm}$). Thus the sum of lengths is $DE + EF = \frac{1}{2}a + \frac{1}{2}a = a\text{ cm}$.

Given is an inscribed triangle $MNQ$, where $O$ is the centre of the circle.

The value of $x$ is
explanation: By the inscribed angle theorem, the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle. The inscribed angle $\angle MNQ = 60^\circ$ is subtended by arc $MQ$. The central angle subtended by the same arc $MQ$ is $x^\circ = 2 \times 60^\circ = 120^\circ$.
